sections.html:
Lamar County lies between Atlanta and Macon, and Barnesville is the seat. It is the fastest growing county in this part of Georgia: the July 2025 estimate of 20,941 residents is 13.2% above the 2020 count, which was 18,500. Land area is 183.50 square miles. Gordon State College and the Barnesville Expo Center give the town some steady local draw, and pecan and peach groves cover much of the farmland.

Prices have moved up with the population. The median owner-home value is $216,500 and the typical commute is the longest around at 31.8 minutes each way. With 136 permits pulled in 2025, an older Lamar County house will be shopped against new construction.

An owner with a mortgage pays a median of $1,469 a month, and one without pays $526. The county has 7,133 households of 2.60 people on average, and 92.5% of residents did not move in the past year.

sections.h2: Property tax offices in Lamar County
sections.html:
Barnesville hosts every office a seller needs.

  • Tax Commissioner: 790 Veteran's Pkwy, Barnesville, GA 30204; mail to P.O. Box 850; phone (770) 358-5162. Walk-in hours are Monday through Thursday, 8 to 4:30, and Friday, 8 to 4:15, with a drive-thru that closes 15 minutes earlier.
  • Tax Assessor, (770) 358-5161: values, appeals and homestead forms, Monday to Thursday 8 to 5 and Friday 8 to 4.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the deed room in the courthouse.

The commissioner's website accepts online payment of property tax and car tag renewals. The commissioner neither sets values nor chooses millage, so a complaint about a high figure goes to the assessors.

Lamar County mails bills by mid-September and wants payment by November 15, a schedule in place since the 2018 tax year. That is five weeks ahead of Georgia's December 20 default, which surprises owners new to the county.

  • Late real estate and business personal property bills collect 1% interest per month.
  • Amounts still open 90 days after the deadline take a 10% penalty.
  • A lien (fifa) goes on file once taxes are over 30 days late, and credit bureaus may see it.
  • Mobile homes are due April 1. Late ones pick up a 10% filing penalty and 1% monthly, and can be auctioned.

State guidance puts the start of interest 60 days after the bill's postmark, so keep the envelope. A refund request for tax paid in error must begin inside three years.

The assessors take forms from January 1 to April 1 and cannot extend the window, so a late filer loses that year. Once approved, an exemption renews itself. Carry a driver license and either your 1040 or a signed income affidavit.

  • State types carry codes: S1 regular homestead, S3 elderly at 62, L4 elderly at 65, S5 disabled veteran and SS surviving spouse of a veteran, the last two requiring VA proof of 100% service-connected disability.
  • Over 65: Lamar takes $20,000 off the county operating levy, nothing else.
  • Over 70: $7,000 comes off school operating tax and school bond tax.
  • Disabled owners: $15,000 off school operating tax when combined household income is under $20,000, documented by two physicians or a Social Security letter that declares 100% disability.

You must meet the state rules before any local break applies. Owners 62 and up with gross household income at or below $15,000 may also defer tax. For a mobile home to count as a homestead, the home and the land under it must have the same owner.

County appraisers lean on recent sales, measured at January 1, and the spring notice shows the result. An owner who objects has 45 days from the notice date and may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. The letter goes to the assessing board and picks a route. Cases that go to the Board of Equalization are heard by a panel the Grand Jury appoints.

Before you file, pull the sales of similar houses near yours and compare them with the value on the notice. The assessors set value as of January 1, so sales close to that date carry the most weight. Put your reasons in the letter, name the route you want, and keep a copy with proof of the mailing date.

Landowners have preferential programs. Lamar cites section 48-5-7.4 for conservation use and residential transitional land, 48-5-7.4.1 for agricultural land and 48-5-7.2 for rehabilitated historic property, and every one asks for a covenant of 10 years or more. Enrolled acreage needs a call to the assessors before the deed changes hands, so a new owner knows what the covenant requires.

Request a payoff that folds in interest and penalty, and check with the Clerk for a recorded fifa. The closing agent pays out of the seller's share and secures the release. January 1 ownership decides who owes the year, so most contracts prorate.

When the owner has died, the county Probate Court can explain how to open the estate before a listing goes up. Cash buyers in Barnesville or the rural parts of the county will still expect the payoff settled at closing.

In practice the steps run in this order. Phone the Tax Commissioner at (770) 358-5162 for the payoff. Ask the Clerk's deed room whether any lien is on record. Have the closing agent pay the commissioner at the table, and keep the receipt for your files.

sections.h2: What to bring to the office
sections.html:
A trip to the Tax Assessor or Tax Commissioner goes faster with a few things in hand. For a homestead filing, bring a driver license and either your 1040 or a signed income affidavit. For a disabled veteran or surviving spouse exemption, bring the VA proof of 100% service-connected disability. For a disabled owner's school break, bring the two physician statements or the Social Security letter.

Buyers who recently closed on a Lamar County house should file their own homestead form before April 1, since the state rules apply first and the local breaks for older owners come after. Owners 62 and up with gross household income at or below $15,000 can ask the assessors how tax deferral works before they list the house.

faqs.q: When is Lamar County property tax due?
faqs.a: November 15. Bills normally go out by September 15, and mobile homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: What do late Lamar County payments cost?
faqs.a: Interest of 1% per month after the due date, plus a 10% penalty at 90 days. A lien can be recorded after 30 days.

faqs.q: Do older Lamar County owners get extra relief?
faqs.a: Yes. Past 65, $20,000 comes off the county operating levy, and past 70, $7,000 comes off school operating and bond tax, once the state rules are met.

faqs.q: What does a typical Lamar County house cost?
faqs.a: About $216,500, the 2020-2024 median for owner-occupied homes. The county had an estimated 20,941 residents in July 2025.

faqs.q: Who accepts Lamar County homestead applications?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor's office, from January 1 through April 1. Bring a driver license and a 1040 or signed income affidavit.
